title: Gilgo Beach Serial Killer Rex Heuermann's 3 Chilling Words Before Furious Judge Delivers His Sentence | TRUTH Press
text:
Gilgo Beach serial killer Rex Heuermann offered three chilling words before a furious Long Island judge handed down three life sentences.
The judge branded the confessed killer of eight women a coward and ordered officers to “get him out of here.”
Killer Speaks in Court Heuermann faced more than a dozen relatives of his victims for the first time Wednesday.
Suffolk County Judge Timothy Mazzei gave him a chance to speak.
“Stand up!” the judge snapped.
“There are no words I can say, but I am responsible for what was said in this room today,” Heuermann told the court.
“The words I would say would have no meaning, and I’m going to leave it there at this time,” he added.
He stood emotionless as several officers hovered near him.
Judge Unloads Mazzei barely contained his disgust as he addressed the killer.
“I know that you’re sorry you got caught,” the judge said.
“Are you a little bit sorry for what you did to these poor innocent women – eight women you strangled to death,” he pressed.
“You’re a disgusting and despicable small man — if you’re a man at all — and you’re a coward,” Mazzei said.
He then turned to the court officers and ordered, “Get him out of here.”
The crowd erupted in cheers, with some chanting “Ogre! Ogre!” as Heuermann was cuffed.
Chilling Torture Methods District Attorney Ray Tierney provided new insight into the killer’s methods.
“When he talks about what he needs to dispose of, he talks about props, toys, wood items,” Tierney said.
He said Heuermann made the wood items himself with family members and used them during the murders.
“He’s treating this as if it were a sport,” the prosecutor said.
“The taking of lives as though it were a sport,” he added.
The grim details prompted one relative to cry out, “I can’t,” before being helped from the room.
A Decades-Long Mystery Heuermann, 62, pleaded guilty in April to the murders.
He admitted strangling and butchering eight sex workers on Long Island between 1993 and 2010.
All but one were killed in a basement “kill room” in his Massapequa Park home.
The bodies were dumped along desolate stretches of Long Island, found starting in December 2010.
The cases remained unsolved for decades until the investigation was reopened in 2022.
A pizza box he tossed outside his Manhattan office helped lead to his arrest the next year.
The Victims Heuermann confessed to killing the four women known as the “Gilgo Four.”
They were Amber Lynn Costello, Megan Waterman, Melissa Barthelemy and Maureen Brainard-Barnes.
He also admitted killing Valerie Mack, Jessica Taylor and Sandra Costilla, his first victim in 1993.
He further copped to the 1996 murder of Karen Vergata.
His lawyer said Heuermann was not involved in two other Gilgo Beach slayings.
Those included Shannon Gilbert and an unidentified victim known only as “Asian Doe.”
Life Behind Bars Heuermann has been held in solitary confinement since his arrest.
He passes the time with books and occasional outdoor time alone in the jailyard.
Sources say he found a sympathetic pen pal in Keith Jesperson, the “Happy Face Killer.”
Jesperson is serving a life sentence and confessed to killing eight women in the 1990s.
He said he advised Heuermann “not to go to trial” after the 2023 arrest.
The three life sentences close out a case that haunted the region for decades.
